The Frozen Window Evaluation Contract (FFW-26) establishes a formalized framework where predictive models are evaluated under frozen conditions—ensuring that all inputs and outputs remain consistent within a defined temporal window. This contract enforces a strict policy on how consensus lines are sourced (via T_emit) and how baselines are constructed (point-in-time refit). The Relative Performance Score (RPS) gate acts as a dual-check mechanism: it compares the model’s performance against a known baseline, ensuring that any improvement is statistically significant. In GSI, this translates to Bayesian updating with frozen priors, while in GSE, it maps to a deterministic state transition governed by performance thresholds. The Pick Emission Contract then takes these calibrated distributions and transforms them into actionable, bettable outcomes using CRPS and other scoring rules. These two primitives together form a closed-loop system where evaluation and emission are tightly coupled, preventing overfitting and ensuring robustness. Failure modes include inconsistent T_emit policies or baseline drift, which would invalidate the freeze and require re-registration.
